rule: waxaana is the focus particle waxaa plus connective -na 'and'. The form itself does not encode a subject person.
source: Morgan Nilsson, Beginner's Somali Grammar / University of Gothenburg, vocabulary note and grammar example
source_example: Waxaana gabi ahaan la xiray waddooyinkaas.
project_execution: Recognize only exact waxaana in an overt second-clause context. Do not infer a hidden subject clitic, antecedent, or verb agreement from the connective particle itself.

rule: waxaana belongs to the waxaa/waxa focus-particle family and is not the person-neutral declarative waana, the statement-clitic wuuna/wayna family, or the baa/ayaa connective-subject-focus family.
source: CONN-WAXAA-001 plus existing project focus/statement distinctions

rule: This executable stage requires waxaa-family connective forms to begin an overt second clause after comma or semicolon. Sentence-initial/discourse-linking forms remain unjudged until broader discourse segmentation is implemented.
source: Reviewed exact forms plus project conservative clause-boundary policy

rule: waxaana, waxayna, and waxaadna are independently reviewed exact forms. Their promotion does not license waxana, waxaanan, waxaynuna, waxaadinna, or any other predicted waxa/waxaa+clitic+-na form.
source: Exact-form evidence plus project no-paradigm-generation policy

rule: waxayna is an independently documented connective cleft-focus form for third-person feminine singular or third-person plural subjects, matching the reviewed ay subject-clitic ambiguity.
source: R. David Zorc, Somali-English Dictionary; independently supported by Morgan Nilsson / University of Gothenburg examples
project_execution: Require an overt preceding clause boundary; check only encoded 3sg_f/3pl compatibility against exact reviewed finite morphology. Do not infer an antecedent or generate related forms.

rule: waxaadna is independently attested as connective 'and you ...'; its base waxaad is documented as focus plus second-person subject pronoun/clitic, matching the reviewed aad 2sg/2pl ambiguity.
source: R. David Zorc, English-Somali Finder List for waxaad; exact waxaadna attested repeatedly in Mahmud Muhammad Abduh's Somali Qur'an translation
source_examples: Waxaadna ku cabbaysaan Biyo kulayl badan.
project_execution: Require an overt preceding clause boundary; check only encoded 2sg/2pl compatibility against exact reviewed finite morphology. Do not infer an antecedent or generate related forms.

rule: For exact waxayna/waxaadna, agreement may be judged only when an exact reviewed finite verb is found in the local predicate window. Unknown predicates remain unjudged. waxaana remains person-neutral and never inherits this agreement rule.
